liner.body_md:
## The recordings

- **gd85-04-08.sbd.wiley.8755.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 147 min; rated 3.97/5 by 34 [1]. Said about its sound: Recording sounds like an audience mic, with crowd energy audible feeding off the band; A delay effect on Jerry's voice is noted as a distinctive sonic feature; Jerry's voice sounds rough, unlike his 1970s performances, though the playing is fine [35][37][42]
- **gd1985-04-08.178658.neumann.km86.bradt.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 147 min [3]
- **gd1985-04-08.149322.senn441.hunt.mattes.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 149 min [5]
- **gd1985-04-08.118481.sbd.healy.damico.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 150 min; rated 2.75/5 by 4 [2]

## Around the show

- Jerry performed a small step and kick in sync with the lyrics during the opener [36]
- Listener and friend took the subway to the Spectrum after hearing WMMR broadcast the show [38]
- Jerry can be heard calling for the song on a good soundboard recording [39]
- Listener notes the song is a treat to watch in video format [43]
- Listener calls the opening of set one a perfect climax to the three-night stand [34]
- Listener prefers this soundboard recording over other available soundboard versions of the show [35]
- Unusual setlist described as very hot, with a solid eleven-song first set [39]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd85-04-08.sbd.wiley.8755.sbeok.shnf**: source: (Healy Mix)SBD>MC>PCM>BETA>DAT>CDR [1]
- **gd1985-04-08.178658.neumann.km86.bradt.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bill Bradt; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Bill Bradt's Master Audience Cassettes: Neumann KM86 mics > Sony D5M (TDK MA-90) [3]
- **gd1985-04-08.149322.senn441.hunt.mattes.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Hunt and Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Rob Hunt and Ted Mattes' Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics > Sony D5M [5]
- **gd1985-04-08.118481.sbd.healy.damico.flac16**: taped by Dan Healy; transferred by Joe D'Amico; source: Soundboard 1st Gen Tape > Tascam 122 mk lll > Korg Mr-1000 > Audio Gate > Cool Edit > Traders Little Helper; Taper : Dan Healy; Editing : Joe D'Amico [2]
